A1.justification: Both PDFs describe StreetCrafter. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching retained material across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: V1 reports original Waymo and PandaSet experiments, conditioning and distillation ablations, sensitivity analyses, and qualitative editing results.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and adds quantitative and qualitative comparisons with ViewCrafter and DriveDreamer4D.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the LiDAR conditioning, diffusion training and inference, and dynamic 3DGS distillation procedure. Shortening the appendix loss descriptions does not establish an objective change. PVG is introduced as a configuration for an additional comparison.

E1.justification: Both versions use Waymo and PandaSet for the same street-view synthesis and editing tasks. The added comparisons use existing input-trajectory and lane-shift scenarios, without extending dataset, domain, or task coverage.

E2.justification: Section 8.1 newly evaluates ViewCrafter against Ours-V and DriveDreamer4D against Ours-G. These methods were previously cited but not directly evaluated. Adding diffusion-based competitors substantially broadens the comparison beyond the retained reconstruction baselines in Tables 1–2.

E3.justification: The added ViewCrafter evaluation constructs geometry from the whole input sequence and fixes DUSt3R camera parameters using dataset calibration. The DriveDreamer4D comparison uses Waymo segment-103593 with PVG as the base model. Existing experimental settings remain unchanged; the FID paragraph supplies previously unstated details.

E4.justification: New Figures 8–10 add qualitative failure-case evidence concerning moving objects, viewpoint extrapolation, and vehicle/building artifacts in the added comparators. The original conditioning and distillation ablations, sampling-ratio and noise-scale analyses, and deformable-object examples are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report aggregate scores without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added table continues averaging across sampled sequences without introducing an uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: V2 adds Table 5: input-trajectory PSNR is 25.90 for Ours-V versus 21.59 for ViewCrafter; 2 m/3 m FID is 62.43/73.49 versus 135.69/137.76. The new single-sequence DriveDreamer4D comparison reports Ours-G FIDs of 89.71/96.11 versus 91.23/123.32. Original main-table and appendix-ablation values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: V1 Appendix A.2 explicitly defines the depth, sky, and object regularization losses in Equations 11–13. V2 Section 7.2 removes these definitions and refers readers to Street Gaussians. Equations 1–10 retain their mathematics; no new assumptions, theorems, or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about precise LiDAR-based camera control, scene editing, and distillation for real-time novel-view rendering. The additional comparisons support these claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: Section 8.1 adds explanations attributing ViewCrafter failures to dynamic geometry and camera-coordinate point clouds, and DriveDreamer4D artifacts to sparse conditioning. These interpretations further motivate world-coordinate LiDAR guidance. StreetCrafter's stated data-collection costs and inference-speed limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 documents FID reference videos and cropping, added baseline adaptations, and nearest-image-plane projection for color assignment. It removes the explicit 95% depth-error pixel selection and Grounded SAM sky-mask details alongside the auxiliary-loss formulas. Training budgets, hardware disclosures, and the code-access link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations to VEGS and Prompting Depth Anything, removes Grounded SAM, and expands the discussion of ViewCrafter and DriveDreamer4D as concurrent work. The broader positioning around LiDAR guidance and dynamic street scenes remains stable.

P1.justification: V2 locally rewrites related work, corrects wording and the Table 5 reference to Table 3 in Section 5.3, adds acknowledgements and corresponding-author information, and reorganizes appendix comparisons. Appendix sections change from A/B to 7/8; the main narrative structure remains intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds Table 5 and Figures 8–10. Existing appendix tables and figures are retained under new numbers and placements, and Figure 4's insets are revised. Most displays and the overall two-column layout remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added comparisons with relevant diffusion-based alternatives provide useful empirical support missing from v1, while the FID clarification improves evaluation transparency. These gains are limited by the single-sequence DriveDreamer4D comparison and partly offset by removing self-contained auxiliary-loss and preprocessing details. With the core method and original results unchanged, the evidence supports a limited overall improvement.
